target_customer: Universities, counseling and social work programs, teletherapy companies, training organizations
problem: Counselors and clinicians have few ways to practice patient conversations at scale before real sessions.
business_model: B2B/B2edu per-institution licence (can be passed to students as a lab fee)
product_category: AI patient simulation for healthcare training

founders.name: Vrishank Saini
founders.background_notes: Founded Bioscope Wellness and Soma Lab; built a mental health app with 120,000+ downloads (YC page).

founders.name: Tiko Bdoyan
founders.background_notes: Former ML researcher (YC page). Launch post names the co-founder 'Tigran', inconsistent with profile.

technical_complexity.rationale: Conversational avatars plus skill feedback built on LLMs; standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Curriculum and LMS integrations help; avatar and LLM approach is copyable.

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand was gathered; the YC page says programs and teletherapy companies use the avatars for training and applicant screening.

rebrands.why: Not sourced; rename stated only on YC page ('formerly Soma Lab')

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name; site promotes moving avatars; no external brand evidence.

outcome_analysis: SimCare, YC S24, is Active with 7 people, formerly Soma Lab, and sells AI client simulations for counselor training with at least one university testimonial. No funding, exit or failure data was found, so this is an early-stage company with unknown outcome.
notes: Rename from Soma Lab appears only on the YC page, not on simcare.ai. Co-founder name mismatch (Tiko vs Tigran) in YC sources. Research limit: the shared WebSearch budget was exhausted before any outcome, funding, competitor or branding search could run, so only the YC page and company site were read; competition_at_founding is left empty (no dated sources), and funding and brand origin facts are unverified or null.
